text: The queue rows, the member rows, the capacity and the reference-load path with its approve and rollback stay with rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1019-APP, -CON, -DB); the rwb-access slice of RWB-AD-014 is the gate in front of them, which ingests the file, checks it whole, records the acceptance and hands it to the owner, and writes no queue field and no queue table.
why: The P4 ownership rows name five tables and none is a queue, the default ruling of R3 gives parameters and reference data to P3, and ASM-A6-api-4 places the reference-load family with rwb-case, so an access-side queue table would contradict the ownership map and the story already carries RWB-P3-E1019-CON as a contract dependency.
read: P4 context pack (service row, ownership rows, REST operations provided); TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.3 and AC-P4-003-01; ASM-A6-api-4; DP-01, DP-11.
confirm: Solution architect and the tech lead of rwb-case
impact: No duplicate queue table and no second load path; the gate depends on the owner's published contract and never on its build, and a change of the queue fields is a change of one contract instead of two services.

text: The gate publishes two operations of its own on base /api/recovery/access/v1: POST /admin/queue-file-checks, which takes the multipart file and its validFrom with a required Idempotency-Key, and GET /admin/queue-file-checks/{checkId}; the five owner operations it consumes keep the owner's paths under /api/recovery/case/v1 and are named by contract id rather than copied.
why: The ownership rows list four rwb-access operations and none of them loads or checks a queue file, the API specification of the TSD places the reference-load family with rwb-case, and the legacy Endpoints table lists the rule-version pair of other stories, so no existing operation can carry this check and no source path exists for it.
read: P4 context pack (REST operations provided: GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants); TSD P4 v3 T-A.1; R4 naming; DP-13.
confirm: Solution architect and the gateway-bff route owner
impact: gateway-bff composes SCR-42 from two calls and the app story builds before the owner's contract is finished; the two paths must be added to the API specification of the service, and a later move would be a breaking change of v1.

text: The check needs the C letter of Reference data, held by RW-COE and RW-REFADM in TSD P4 T6.1, and the read needs the R letter of the same area; the legacy row that gives the load the R and A letters of Rules and parameters is not carried for the load, and the caller's right is read from permission at the version in force.
why: TSD P4 T6.1 is the only source with a rights matrix for P4 and it holds the load letters in Reference data, while the legacy Permission checks table names Rules and parameters for a rule-version operation that belongs to RWB-AD-011 and RWB-AD-012 and not to a queue file.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and T6.2; legacy RWB-AD-014 Permission checks table; FSD P4 v3 A2.3.3.3 roles and permissions; REQ-ACA-003.
confirm: Security administrator and the compliance officer
impact: The reference data administrator can run the check and the security administrator can read it; a role that holds only Rules and parameters R cannot check a queue file, which is a visible change from the monolith and is recorded here rather than hidden.

text: The approval of a queue version, the rule that the author cannot approve it and the MSG-P7-002 refusal stay with the owner's approve operation, where the legacy row gives the A letter of Rules and parameters to RW-RISK; the gate never approves, never rolls back and only reports the owner's answer.
why: TSD P4 T6.1 grants no A letter in Reference data and names RW-RISK with RA in Rules and parameters, the legacy permission row gives the approval to RW-RISK, and the owner holds the version that the approval moves, so an approval in the gate would need a second copy of the version state.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.1; legacy RWB-AD-014 Permission checks table; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-003-01; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 (API-P4-006).
confirm: Risk and the tech lead of rwb-case
impact: One approver check and one MSG-P7-002 in the system instead of two; the gate shows the owner's approval state and cannot disagree with it.

text: The two queue columns the legacy Data table leaves as "and 2 more" are read as capacity_cap (DF-WRK-007) and overflow_queue_code (DF-WRK-008); the eight file columns are id, queue_code, queue_name, team_code, role_code, assignment_method, capacity_cap and overflow_queue_code.
why: The legacy text names only six of the eight fields, the capacity and the overflow queue are the two behaviours the legacy criteria and FSD AC-ALT-P4-003-02 test, and no other queue field is named anywhere in the documents read for this WP.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-014 Data table and AC2; FSD P4 v3 AC-P4-003-01 and AC-ALT-P4-003-02; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 (DF-REF-054 target_queue_code).
confirm: The data steward and the tech lead of rwb-case
impact: The file, the finding fields and the test data use one name per column; a different name in the owner's physical schema is a rename of a field in the document, not a change of a rule.

text: The file the gate checks is one queue sheet with a header row and the eight columns of ASM-B2-P4-008-5; a QUEUE_MEMBER sheet in the same file is passed to the owner untouched, because queue_member is rwb-case's table and its columns and its member checks are not in the documents read for this WP.
why: FSD AC-P4-003-01 loads a QUEUE and a QUEUE_MEMBER sheet of 48 rows together while the legacy story names only a queue file, and a member check in the gate would need the member columns and the user identities that no source read for this WP gives.
read: FSD P4 v3 AC-P4-003-01; legacy RWB-AD-014 Story and Data table; ASM-A6-api-4.
confirm: The tech lead of rwb-case and the reference data administrator role
impact: The gate validates every queue rule it owns and leaves member validity to the owner of the member table; a member error is then found by the owner's load and not by the gate, which the screen must say.

text: The caseload cap maximum is a parameters row of rwb-case read with the version in force through its parameters contract, and its key, its value and its unit are the owner's; the gate carries no numeric cap, applies no default and refuses a cap only when it is a whole number above zero and above the parameter in force.
why: DL23 makes the cap a parameter and principle 1 forbids a business value in code, while no source read for this WP names the key or the value; a default would silently change a workload limit.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.3.3.1 (BR-P4-003); legacy RWB-AD-014 Decision DL23 and Data table (DF-WRK-007); DP-06.
confirm: The product head of the cap policy and the data steward
impact: A cap change is a parameters change with no deployment; the document and the validator need the key name before build, and until then the check reads the maximum with the version in force and names the key as the owner's.

text: The seven finding codes OVERFLOW_QUEUE_UNKNOWN, ROLE_UNKNOWN, TEAM_UNKNOWN, ASSIGNMENT_METHOD_UNKNOWN, CAP_ABOVE_PARAMETER, DUPLICATE_QUEUE_CODE and VALID_FROM_IN_PAST are this run's names for the rules the sources state in words, each of severity Error, and each carries the queue field name it fails on.
why: The legacy criteria and the FSD rules state the refusals in words and no source gives a code list, so a caller cannot bind to a code that no document fixes; naming them once in the contract story keeps the gate and the screen in step.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-014 AC2; FSD P4 v3 AC-P4-003-01, AC-ALT-P4-003-02, AC-EXC-P4-003-01, AC-EXC-P4-003-02; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12.
confirm: Solution architect and the QA lead
impact: One vocabulary for the answer, the screen and the tests; adding a code is additive within v1 and removing one needs a new major version.

text: The acceptance entry of DP-03 is written with the decision code the owner's reference-load operation records, with no case id and with the check id as its subject, and its outbox row travels to rwb.decision-record.v1 through the platform library; the gate publishes nothing on rwb.access.events.v1.
why: The sources fix that an accepted administration change is recorded before it takes effect (R-UNI-39, legacy TC-AD-014-04) and that the queue version is the owner's, but no source gives the decision code of a queue-file check and a queue file belongs to no case.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-014 Test case TC-AD-014-04 and Validation and messages (MSG-P7-003); FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-003-08; DP-03; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (the record of an administrative change).
confirm: The compliance officer and the platform library owner
impact: The record exists for every acceptance and is queryable with the decision log; the code is a label the owner already uses, so no new code list is introduced and no case-level audit changes.
